summary_paragraph: A woman with complex bariatric surgical history (prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with later reversal) complicated by chronic abdominal pain and post-prandial hypoglycemia requiring prior dextrose infusions via PICC, and a seizure disorder on levetiracetam, was admitted after a witnessed ~3-minute seizure with fever, leukocytosis, elevated lactate, and fluid-responsive hypotension concerning for sepsis. Imaging showed left lower lobe pneumonia and no acute intra-abdominal process. Blood cultures grew coagulase-negative Staphylococcus (Staph epidermidis) in one bottle, raising concern for central-line associated bloodstream infection; the PICC was removed (tip culture without significant growth), Infectious Diseases recommended a 7-day course of IV vancomycin, repeat surveillance cultures remained negative, and transthoracic echocardiogram showed no valvular vegetations. Neurology increased levetiracetam to 1000 mg twice daily. Endocrinology and Nutrition evaluated hypoglycemia and malnutrition risk, attributing symptoms to post-prandial hypoglycemia exacerbated by high-glycemic foods; diet was advanced to a diabetic/consistent-carbohydrate plan with small frequent meals and Glucerna supplementation, and glucose remained stable without ongoing D5 infusions despite intermittent severe abdominal pain requiring breakthrough hydromorphone. She was discharged home hemodynamically stable, tolerating small meals, with close neurology and endocrinology/nutrition follow-up and bowel regimen and opioid safety planning.
